questions.prompt: State the cofactor expansion formula along row 1 for a \(3\times 3\) matrix \(A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&c\\d&e&f\\g&h&i\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: Expanding along row 1 gives \(\det(A)\) = \(a\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}e&f\\h&i\end{pmatrix}\right)\) - \(b\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}d&f\\g&i\end{pmatrix}\right)\) + \(c\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}d&e\\g&h\end{pmatrix}\right)\). The signs alternate plus, minus, plus across the first row.

The minor M_13 is found by deleting row 1 and column 3. The remaining \(2\times 2\) matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\6&7\end{pmatrix}\). Its determinant is \(3\cdot7\) - \(4\cdot6\) = 21 - 24 = -3. Therefore \(M_13=-3\).
The cofactor is C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij. From the previous minor calculation, \(M_13=-3\). Since (-1)^(1+3) = (-1)^4 = 1, \(C_13=1\)*(-3) = -3.

Column 2 is \((0,1,0)\), so only the middle entry contributes. The sign at row 2 column 2 is positive. Delete row 2 and column 2 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\5&6\end{pmatrix}\). Its determinant is \(1\cdot6\) - \(2\cdot5\) = 6 - 10 = -4. Therefore the determinant is -4.

Expand along row 1. The first term is zero. The second term has a minus sign: -\(2\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\5&0\end{pmatrix}\right)\) = -2*(\(3\cdot0\) - \(4\cdot5\)) = -2*(-20) = 40. The third term is +\(1\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\5&6\end{pmatrix}\right)\) = 1*(18 - 0) = 18. Therefore \(\\det=40\) + 18 = 58.

questions.prompt: Choose the best row or column for cofactor expansion of \(\begin{pmatrix}4&0&0\\1&2&3\\5&0&6\end{pmatrix}\), and compute the determinant.
questions.answer: Column 2 is best because it has two zeros: \((0,2,0)\). Only the entry 2 in row 2 contributes. Its sign is positive because row 2 plus column 2 is even. Delete row 2 and column 2 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}4&0\\5&6\end{pmatrix}\). The minor determinant is \(4\cdot6\) - \(0\cdot5\) = 24. Therefore \(\\det=2\)*24 = 48.

questions.prompt: For a \(4\times 4\) matrix, what size is the minor matrix obtained by deleting one row and one column?
questions.answer: Deleting one row from a \(4\times 4\) matrix leaves 3 rows. Deleting one column leaves 3 columns. Therefore each minor matrix is \(3\times 3\).

questions.prompt: Explain the sign pattern for cofactors in a \(3\times 3\) determinant.
questions.answer: The cofactor sign at position \((i, j)\) is (-1)^(i+j). For a \(3\times 3\) matrix this gives the checkerboard pattern \(\begin{pmatrix}+&-&+\\-&+&-\\+&-&+\end{pmatrix}\). Adjacent signs alternate across rows and down columns.

Expand along row 1: \(\\det=1\)*\(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}5&6\\8&9\end{pmatrix}\right)\) - \(2\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}4&6\\7&9\end{pmatrix}\right)\) + \(3\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}4&5\\7&8\end{pmatrix}\right)\). The minors are \(5\cdot9\) - \(6\cdot8\) = -3, \(4\cdot9\) - \(6\cdot7\) = -6, and \(4\cdot8\) - \(5\cdot7\) = -3. Therefore \(\\det=1\)*(-3) - 2*(-6) + 3*(-3) = -3 + 12 - 9 = 0.

questions.prompt: A learner expands along row 1 but uses all plus signs. Explain why this is wrong for a \(3\times 3\) determinant.
questions.answer: Cofactor expansion includes signs determined by (-1)^(i+j). Along row 1, the signs are plus, minus, plus. The middle term must be subtracted. Using all plus signs ignores the cofactor sign pattern and can give the wrong determinant.
